recognize_zh: 箭頭指的紅血球邊緣缺了一塊、像被咬掉一口（bite cell），上方另有一顆紅血球邊緣有空洞樣缺口，提示氧化性溶血（如 G6PD 缺乏）。
features: Red cell (arrow) with a sharply demarcated semicircular peripheral defect, as if a bite had been removed
Additional red cell above with an eccentric notch/vacuole-like defect near its membrane (bite or blister form)
Remaining red cells are normocytic with central pallor; mild anisocytosis
No spherocytes, schistocytes or target cells prominent in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows mostly normocytic red cells with preserved central pallor. The arrowed red cell has a smooth, semicircular peripheral indentation characteristic of a bite cell (degmacyte), and a second red cell shows a similar eccentric membrane defect. Fragmented red cells and spherocytes are not prominent in this field. Findings are suggestive of oxidative hemolysis with splenic removal of Heinz bodies, as in G6PD deficiency or unstable hemoglobin; a Heinz body preparation and G6PD assay are recommended.

ddx.vs: Helmet cells have straight, angular cut edges with pointed horns, whereas bite cells have a rounded concave defect.
Blister cells retain a thin membrane rim over a peripheral vacuole, while a true bite cell has the membrane completely removed.
Keratocytes show two horn-like projections flanking a notch rather than a single smooth bite.
